claims.text: The baseline is a homogeneous, single-phase high-entropy alloy without engineered nanoscale precipitates.
Targeted alloying additions and/or specialized heat treatment can introduce nanoscale intermetallic precipitates into the baseline alloy.
The intervention will produce stabilized nanoscale intermetallic precipitates within the matrix.
The intervention will produce stabilized nanoscale intermetallic precipitates at or near grain boundaries.
The nanoscale precipitates will inhibit grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
The nanoscale precipitates will restrict dynamic recrystallization at elevated temperature.
Inhibition of grain-boundary sliding and dynamic recrystallization will enhance creep resistance.
Inhibition of grain-boundary sliding and dynamic recrystallization will help maintain yield strength at high temperature.
At approximately 800°C, the precipitate-engineered alloy will have higher yield strength than the unmodified homogeneous alloy.
At approximately 800°C, the precipitate-engineered alloy will have a lower creep rate than the unmodified homogeneous alloy.
The anticipated benefit applies during prolonged exposure near 800°C under extreme environmental loading.
Conditions around 800°C are representative of aerospace turbine applications.
The benefits may not extend to significantly lower temperatures or less aggressive service conditions.
Precipitate coarsening during sustained high-temperature exposure may prevent the alloy from retaining the predicted mechanical benefits.
